newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae sets largest global NewZealand dlr bond.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae sets largest global NewZealand dlr bond.

text.p: Fannie Mae launched the first New Zealand dollar bond for a U.S. agency on Friday which saw broad-based sales distribution and will trade as a liquid benchmark, a Fannie Mae official said.

"The bond is the first New Zealand dollar deal ever done by a U.S. agency and the largest non-government New Zealand dollar deal," Fannie Mae's director of long-term funding Mehmood Nathani told Reuters.
"New Zealand dollars also met our funding targets in the swap market," he added.
The NZ$500 million ($340 million) five-year bond was priced to yield 21 basis points over the March 2002 New Zealand government bond.
Joint lead managers for the transaction were Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Toronto-Dominion.

"We've been surprised with the global distribution and the combined split is around 43 percent into the U.S., 30 percent into Asia and 30 percent into Europe," syndicate manager at Toronto Dominion said.
He said there was predominantly institutional demand with some retail interest.
"New Zealand is diminishing its domestic debt and paying down government debt very quickly, so there is the need for a large liquid deal to replace the shortage," he added.
